euler-line.translation: Collinear axis of X(4), X(5), X(2), X(3)
euler-line.definition: The straight line discovered by Euler in E325 (§§ 16–18, 1765/1767) passing through the orthocenter E = X(4), centroid F = X(2), and circumcenter H = X(3) with ratio EF : FH = 2 : 1, and bisecting segment EH at the nine-point center L = X(5).

nine-point-circle.headword: Nine-Point Circle (Kreis durch die Fußpunkte der Perpendikel)
nine-point-circle.definition: The circle of radius R/2 centered at the midpoint L = X(5) of the orthocenter-circumcenter segment, passing through the three altitude feet, the three side midpoints, and the three Euler midpoints toward the orthocenter (Feuerbach 1822, §§ 26, 54–56, 9. Satz).

feuerbach-point.definition: The unique point of internal tangency between the nine-point circle and the incircle of a non-equilateral triangle, proved by Feuerbach in § 57 via LS = |R/2 - r|.

tritangent-circles.definition: The four circles tangent to all three extended sides of a triangle: the internal incircle (center S = X(1), radius r) and the three external excircles (centers S', S'', S''', radii r', r'', r''').

orthic-triangle.definition: The triangle MNP formed by the orthogonal feet of the three altitudes of ABC; for an acute triangle, its incenter is the orthocenter O = X(4) and its inradius is rho = 2R cos(alpha) cos(beta) cos(gamma) (Feuerbach §§ 19–25).

feuerbach-triangle.translation: Excircle tangency triangle Fea Feb Fec
feuerbach-triangle.definition: The triangle inscribed in the nine-point circle whose vertices are the three points of external tangency between the nine-point circle and the three excircles of ABC.

quadrance.definition: The exact polynomial invariant Q(A, B) = (x_B - x_A)^2 + (y_B - y_A)^2 eliminating irrational square roots in metric geometry, employed systematically throughout Euler (1765) and Feuerbach (1822).

harmonic-range.definition: Four collinear points whose projective cross-ratio equals -1; along the Euler line, the nine-point center X(5) and circumcenter X(3) divide the segment between the orthocenter X(4) and centroid X(2) internally and externally in ratio 3 : 1.

casus-irreducibilis.definition: The algebraic phenomenon identified at the close of Euler's E325 (§ 34, p. 123) in which reconstructing the three real positive sides (a, b, c) from z^3 - pz^2 + qz - r = 0 requires complex intermediate cube roots or angle trisection.

symmetric-polynomials.definition: Euler's symmetric generators p = a + b + c, q = ab + ac + bc, and r = abc (§ 10, p. 107; note that in Euler 1765 r denotes the product abc rather than the inradius).
